I don't know enough about the specifics of bulking-cutting to have much an opinion other than from what I can deduce with my undergrad degree. At my own gut instinct I am against it, but with no research to back myself. Nor do I have any research to say it's good.

More or less, who here can scientifically prove to me one way or another, that there is a reason to bulk/cut? Even if there is no decisive do or don't, being able to see views that I don't have will help me to piece it together.
Hey guys, I want to know your opinions on bulking and cutting.

What are you trying to accomplish? If you are against bulking/cutting what are you in favor of? If you are trying to gain muscle you are going to need to have a calorie surplus. Inevitably this will lead to some fat gain as well. It's not possible to only put on lean muscle mass. Therefore, you would eventually need to cut to eliminate the extra fat gain.

Assuming your goal is to increase muscle mass, I don't see any way around the bulk/cut if you want to make serious progress. That being said, there are many ways to go about doing it. This article is pretty good at going in depth on the different options.

http://rippedbody.jp/nutritional-hierarchy-importance-calories/

Wait what? How can you be against cutting and bulking it's literally either gaining more muscles than fat through eating more or losing less muscles than fat through eating less to increase LBM. Are you confusing bulk/cut cycles with something else?

I don't believe so. It makes 0 sense to me from a biological standpoint why you would need to add fat, visible fat, in order to increase muscle mass. Fat doesn't just add subcutaneously, it will add to the lining of organs, inside your layers of muscle fiber, arteries, veins, everywhere.

If anything, I'm mostly wondering why people don't eat a slight caloric excess each day they want to gain to make up for their workouts and then cut back slightly to shed the (hopefully) little fat they put on. Further, because our bodies go through protein catabolism before burning fat, as muscle is a huge energy waste biologically (and our bodies don't enjoy using energy where it isn't necessary) fat is harder to burn than muscle is to grow.

All I really want is a scientific reason why a bulk/cut is necessary or even better than simply building muscle in what I can only describe as a lean bulk currently.

You don't want to add fat it's just a byproduct of eating at a surplus while loading enough protein and giving stimulus to promote muscle growth.

And just eating a slight caloric excess is really hard because you'd have to do that track for a way longer time than you would have to if you were to do a slow bulk (50 calories vs 250 calories means 5 times slower/faster bulk/cut) and any deviation from the caloric goal has bigger impact. That is IF you gain any muscle during as your body wants a certain amount of bf% before he wants to spend the extra energy available for additional muscle cells.

Now the advantages for a normal bulk/cut cycle is that it is a lot faster and more controllable, plus fat gain promotes a higher muscle gain as well.

And fat is not harder to burn than muscle is to grow given the right conditions because if it were bulk/cut cycles would not work at all since bodybuilders use it all the time. What people do is give muscles appropriate stimuli (Training) to counteract the normal response, this is why cuts work.

I don't know what degree you have, but I assume it's not biology-related, so it was just from the classes you had to take as requirements.

The body has metabolic process that affect multiple (if not all) organs, including subcutaneous fat and/or muscle. When you drink a pill, do you think that it was designed to only reach it's target organ? blood flows everywhere, and usually a pill affects the whole body. Catabolism and anabolism are processes that never stop, just change their speeds; there are even metabolic pathways described as 'amphibolic' which have both catabolic and anabolic components. Most likely the classes you took gave simplified information.

But all of that is not too important. Search pubmed for scientific papers on the effectiveness bulking/cutting if you want them; they might not describe the mechanism, but they will give as much scientific proof as possible that bulking/cutting works.

That being said, it's perfectly possible to add muscle without fat, however, due to shared chemical reactions between muscle anabolism and fat catabolism, it's much slower than a bulk/cut cycle, though it does have it's uses, mainly for models who need to have an 8 pack all year round, but still want to gain muscle.

Hello, I have to politely inform you that the terms you’re laying out are a nightmare for any designer/developer.

Even if someone was passionate and generous and willing to help you for free, the fact that you don’t want to commit any of your own ideas first, but want to add them later, is stifling for creative work.

This is the nightmare scenario:

What colour should the thing be?

Design it and I’ll chuck in my own ideas later.

(designs the thing in red) How about red?

I hate red.

What colour do you like then?

I don’t want to influence the creative process! You choose.

(redesigns the thing in blue) How about blue?

I hate blue.

Just tell me what colour you want.

No, I want a designer who can work without my input.

Working for free is a give-and-take. You can ask someone to work for free, but in return you have to value their time. You can’t ask 5 people to give you their time for free and say "I only value the time of one of you, but I can’t tell you which one until after you spend that time. It’ll be a surprise!” (Well you can, but that’s not a good use of anyone’s time.)

Surely you have some preferences of your own. Start with broad ideas: do you want it light or dark themed, do you want it to look fun or formal, do you like certain colours, do you dislike certain colours. It will help anyone who is helping you greatly.
